claims.claim: Tesla's Wardenclyffe tower was dynamited for scrap
claims.quote: On July 4, 1917, the Smiley Steel Company of New York began demolition of the tower by dynamiting it.

claims.claim: The site was in Shoreham, Long Island
claims.quote: Wardenclyffe is located near the Shoreham Post Office and Shoreham Fire House on Route 25A in Shoreham, Long Island, New York.

claims.claim: The tower never became operational
claims.quote: Additional investment could not be found, and the project was abandoned in 1906, never to become operational.

claims.claim: The card 1 photograph shows Wardenclyffe circa 1902
claims.quote: Description: Tesla's Wardenclyffe plant on Long Island in partial stage of completion. ... Circa 1902

claims.claim: The 1904 photograph was taken so Tesla could go back to J. P. Morgan and ask for the funds to finish the tower
claims.quote: This 1904 photo of Wardenclyffe was taken so that Tesla could go back to J. P. Morgan to try and get the additional funds he needed to finish the tower.

claims.claim: Morgan had already refused to provide additional funds before 1904
claims.quote: With Tesla basically proposing a breach of contract, Morgan refused to lend additional funds and demanded an account of money already spent.

claims.claim: Tesla wanted to make the Earth itself resonate
claims.quote: He theorized from these experiments that if he injected electric current into the Earth at just the right frequency he could harness what he believed was the planet's own electrical charge and cause it to resonate at a frequency that would be amplified in "standing waves"

claims.claim: Tesla doubted radio waves (Hertzian waves) were the answer
claims.quote: Tesla discarded the idea of using the newly discovered Hertzian waves (radio waves), detected in 1888 by German physicist Heinrich Rudolf Hertz. Tesla doubted they existed

claims.claim: Tesla planned to inject current into the ground and return it through a charged upper layer of the atmosphere
claims.quote: His system was based more on 19th-century ideas of electrical conduction and telegraphy instead of the newer theories of electromagnetic waves, with an electrical charge being conducted through the ground and being returned through the air.

claims.claim: US patent 1,119,732 is a Tesla patent related to Wardenclyffe
claims.quote: "Apparatus for Transmitting Electrical Energy", January 18, 1902, U.S. patent 1,119,732, December 1, 1914

claims.claim: Beneath the tower there was a shaft sunk 120 feet into the ground, wood and steel lined, with a stairway inside
claims.quote: the facility had a ten by twelve foot wood and steel lined shaft sunk into the ground 120 feet (37 m) beneath the tower with a stairway inside it

claims.claim: From the bottom of the shaft Tesla pushed iron pipes out 300 feet
claims.quote: I pushed these iron pipes, I think sixteen of them, three hundred feet, and then the current through these pipes takes hold of the earth.

claims.claim: Tesla said the purpose was "to have a grip on the earth"
claims.quote: In Tesla's words, the function of this was "to have a grip on the earth so the whole of this globe can quiver".

claims.claim: The first dynamite blast only tilted the tower
claims.quote: The tower was knocked on a tilt by the initial explosion but it was not totally demolished until September.

claims.claim: The Smiley Steel Company began dynamiting on July 4, 1917
claims.quote: On July 4, 1917, the Smiley Steel Company of New York began demolition of the tower by dynamiting it.

claims.claim: The tower was not fully down until September
claims.quote: The tower was knocked on a tilt by the initial explosion but it was not totally demolished until September.

claims.claim: The scrap value realized was $1,750
claims.quote: The scrap value realized was $1,750 (equivalent to $44,000 in 2025).

claims.claim: The 1917 demolition photograph is attributed to the American Press Association
claims.quote: Author: attributed to the "American Press Association"

claims.claim: Four 100-foot passages are described as running north, south, east and west from the bottom of the shaft
claims.quote: There is also contemporaneous and later descriptions of four 100 foot long tunnels, possibly brick lined and waterproofed, radiating from the bottom of the shaft north, south, east, and west terminating back at ground level in little brick igloos.

claims.claim: Accounts disagree on whether the tunnels were for drainage, access, or part of the ground connection
claims.quote: Speculation on the tunnels ranges from them being for drainage, acting as access ways, or having the function of enhancing ground connection or resonance by interacting with the water table below the tower

claims.claim: How Tesla meant to combine ground conduction with the atmospheric method is unknown
claims.quote: How Tesla intended to employ the ground conduction method and atmospheric method in Wardenclyffe's design is unknown.

claims.claim: The card 6 image is a 1904 photograph of Wardenclyffe
claims.quote: Archive title: File:Wardenclyffe Tower - 1904.jpg

claims.claim: In 1901 J. P. Morgan gave Tesla $150,000 for a wireless station on Long Island capable of reaching London and ships at sea
claims.quote: Morgan signed a contract with Tesla in March 1901, agreeing to give the inventor $150,000 ($5.81 million in 2025) to develop and build a wireless station on Long Island, capable of sending wireless messages to London as well as ships at sea.

claims.claim: Morgan took 51% of the company and its patents
claims.quote: The deal also included Morgan having a 51% interest in the company as well as a 51% share in present and future wireless patents developed from the project.

claims.claim: Tesla read that Marconi was sending signals over the horizon
claims.quote: Tesla's plans changed radically after he read a June 1901 Electrical Review article by Marconi titled "Syntonic Wireless Telegraph". At this point, Marconi was transmitting radio signals beyond the range most physicists thought possible (over the horizon)

claims.claim: Tesla decided to scale up with a bigger transmitter, image and telephone transmission, and wireless power, and asked Morgan for more money; Morgan refused
claims.quote: decided to scale up his designs with a much more powerful transmitter, incorporating his ideas of advanced telephone and image transmission as well as his ideas of wireless power delivery.

claims.claim: The tower was a 187-foot wood tower
claims.quote: By the end of 1902 the tower reached its full height of 187 feet.

claims.claim: The cupola weighed 55 tons
claims.quote: It had a 55-ton steel (some report it was a better conducting material, such as copper) hemispherical structure at the top (referred to as a cupola).

claims.claim: In July 1903, on the night Morgan refused in writing, newspapers reported the tower shooting flashes into the night sky
claims.quote: The night of Morgan's reply, and several nights after, newspapers reported that the Wardenclyffe tower came alive shooting off bright flashes lighting up the night sky.

claims.claim: No explanation was given for the flashes
claims.quote: No explanation was forthcoming from Tesla or any of his workers as to the meaning of the display and Wardenclyffe never seemed to operate again.

claims.claim: Tesla's mortgage was held by the proprietor of the Waldorf-Astoria, where he lived
claims.quote: In 1904, Tesla took out a mortgage on the Wardenclyffe property with George C. Boldt, proprietor of the Waldorf-Astoria Hotel, to cover Tesla's living expenses at the hotel.

claims.claim: Tesla owed about $20,000 at the Waldorf-Astoria
claims.quote: By 1915, Tesla's accumulated debt at the Waldorf-Astoria was around US$20,000 (equivalent to $637,000 in 2025).

claims.claim: Foreclosure followed
claims.quote: When Tesla was unable to make any further payments on the mortgages, Boldt foreclosed on the Wardenclyffe property.

claims.claim: A wartime rumour said the government ordered the tower down over German spies
claims.quote: a rumor spread, picked up by newspapers and other publications, that the tower was demolished on orders of the United States Government with claims German spies were using it as a radio transmitter or observation post

claims.claim: The rumour was false
claims.quote: Tesla was not pleased with what he saw as attacks on his patriotism via the rumors about Wardenclyffe, but since the original mortgages with Boldt as well as the foreclosure had been kept off the public record in order to hide his financial difficulties, Tesla was not able to reveal the real reason for the demolition.

claims.claim: The mortgages were kept off the public record, so Tesla could not give the real reason
claims.quote: since the original mortgages with Boldt as well as the foreclosure had been kept off the public record in order to hide his financial difficulties, Tesla was not able to reveal the real reason for the demolition

claims.claim: All the photographs used are public domain
claims.quote: Licence: Public domain

claims.claim: The four tunnels radiated from the tower's base and the question is still unresolved
claims.quote: Speculation on the tunnels ranges from them being for drainage, acting as access ways, or having the function of enhancing ground connection or resonance by interacting with the water table below the tower
